read: The biggest story is political, not clinical. Early AP counts show Democrats taking both chambers of Congress, which moves drug pricing back into play: expect IRA expansion bills, hearings on the MFN deals and more PBM scrutiny, although a Trump veto limits what actually becomes law. On fundamentals, big-cap earnings keep beating and raising (Novo this morning, Pfizer and Amgen yesterday), but share reactions are flat to negative. After the late-October healthcare rally, a lot of that strength looks priced in. Lower down the market, the tone is risk-off: Servier's $1.55bn sevasemten bet failed its pivotal trial, Ultragenyx is cutting a fifth of its staff, and BioNTech's ADC and vaccine data were mixed. Capital is still going to obesity and late-stage, de-risked assets and to China/Asia-sourced molecules, while rare-disease gene therapy keeps contracting.

items.headline: US midterms: Democrats win the House and Senate, putting drug pricing back on the legislative agenda
items.detail: AP counts early Wednesday show at least 53 Senate seats and 220 House seats for Democrats, with votes still being counted. The likely first moves are oversight of the MFN deals, pressure to expand or speed up IRA negotiation, and PBM reform. Pfizer's Bourla says he expects no change to the MFN agreements, which run through Trump's term. This looks like a multiple headwind for US-heavy pharma rather than an immediate earnings hit.

items.headline: Novo Nordisk Q3: beat and raise; Wegovy pill does DKK 5.4bn in the quarter; DKK 4.6bn ziltivekimab impairment
items.detail: Sales were DKK 79.2bn (+4% CER) and adjusted operating profit was DKK 31.7bn (+27% CER, flattered by Q3 2025 transformation costs). 2026 guidance for adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit is now −2% to +2% CER. Reported operating profit fell 9% CER after DKK 8.7bn of impairments: DKK 4.6bn on ziltivekimab, which is a negative read for the IL-6 CV-inflammation thesis, and DKK 4.1bn on the manufacturing network. CagriSema US launch is planned for early 2027.

items.headline: Pfizer Q3: beat and raise on Eliquis and oncology; shares slip
items.detail: Revenue was $16.58bn against $15.87bn consensus, and adjusted EPS of $0.87 beat by $0.14. 2026 revenue guidance rises to $62–64bn (from $60.5–62.5bn) and EPS to $2.95–3.05 (from $2.80–3.00). Eliquis grew 25% to $2.52bn on US net price, and Padcev was strong. Shares were down about 1% midday. The next real catalyst is the Metsera amylin data.

items.headline: Amgen Q3: clean beat and guidance raise, but the stock waits for MariTide
items.detail: Revenue was $10.4bn (+8%, about $10.1bn expected) and adjusted EPS was $6.45 against $5.79 expected. FY revenue guidance moves to $38.9–39.7bn (from $38.2–39.4bn) and EPS to $22.90–23.70 (from $22.30–23.50). Repatha did $1.09bn (+37%); Prolia fell 45% to $632m on biosimilars. Shares were down more than 2% after hours. The first MariTide Phase 3 data arrive in 2027.

items.headline: Servier's sevasemten fails the pivotal GRAND CANYON trial in Becker muscular dystrophy, five months after a $1.55bn buyout
items.detail: There was no significant benefit on NSAA and the secondary endpoints also missed; safety was clean. The result contradicts the Phase 2 CANYON signal. Servier paid Edgewise $1.55bn cash plus about $1bn in milestones, which now look impaired. It is another warning on functional endpoints in slow-progressing muscular dystrophies.

items.headline: BioNTech Q3: revenue guidance midpoint raised; ADC and vaccine data mixed
items.detail: Revenue was €1.29bn and IFRS net profit €184.5m. FY revenue guidance is now €1.7–1.9bn (from €1.6–1.9bn), with €16.2bn of cash. Trastuzumab pamirtecan (DualityBio) met PFS in DYNASTY-Breast02, but the benefit was modest and ILD rates were higher, so BLA plans are under review. BNT113 missed PFS. The adjuvant CRC trial of autogene cevumeran is being stopped early. A new Gilead collaboration will test pumitamig plus Trodelvy in first-line PD-L1-low TNBC.

items.headline: Ultragenyx cuts about 20% of staff and ends the UX701 Wilson disease gene therapy
items.detail: Headcount falls to about 1,000 in its second cut this year, and the GTX-102 Angelman studies are being wound down. 2027 R&D is guided below $350m. Cash was $401m at the end of Q3, plus about $350m net from two PRV sales. The 2026 revenue guide of $730–760m is reaffirmed.

items.headline: Vertex falls about 3% after Q3 as investors weigh the povetacicept launch risk
items.detail: Revenue was $3.44bn (+12%), with Alyftrek at $706m (a beat) and Journavx at $58m (a miss). EPS was 4% below consensus, and revenue guidance was nudged up to $13.15–13.25bn. An FDA decision on pove in IgAN is expected by the end of November, with a citizen's petition on antibody-level monitoring hanging over it.

items.headline: Merck KGaA sells its US CDMO network to Lonza
items.detail: The deal covers five sites (bioconjugates, HPAPI linkers, viral vectors, LNP and fill-finish) and about 1,100 staff. The price is near the midpoint of a CHF 100–600m range, and the sites should bring about CHF 250m of sales in 2028. Closing is expected mid-2027. Merck KGaA keeps narrowing its life-science portfolio, and Lonza doubles its US footprint.

items.headline: Minghui licenses Japan rights to its Phase 3 IGF-1R antibody for thyroid eye disease to ASKA for $110m upfront
items.detail: The deal is worth up to $440m in total for MHB018A. A $110m upfront for Japan-only rights is rich and shows how much Chinese licensors' pricing power has grown.

items.headline: Madrigal Q3: Rezdiffra $431m (+50% y/y), now profitable
items.detail: More than 55,850 patients are on therapy and net income was $55.4m. A new Phase 3 outcomes trial in compensated cirrhosis (MAESTRO-CSPH, more than 2,000 patients) starts in H1 2027, and Madrigal has 18 abstracts at AASLD this week.

items.headline: Teva raises its outlook for Austedo, Ajovy and Uzedy after their combined sales grow 33%
items.detail: Combined Q3 sales were about $1.1bn. Separately, Teva licensed US rights to Samsung Bioepis' infliximab and etanercept biosimilars, with undisclosed upfront and profit-share terms.

items.headline: Dr. Reddy's wins FDA tentative approval for the first generic lenacapavir (PrEP)
items.detail: It will cost $40 per person per year in the 120 LMICs covered by Gilead's voluntary licence, with first supply by the end of 2026. There is no impact on Gilead's US franchise.

items.headline: Bayer's CEO says the company is "working on" a US MFN deal
items.detail: That would be one more major company inside the MFN framework before Congress changes hands.

items.headline: Two new VC firms close first funds: Aulis Capital ($200m) and NeoSci Ventures ($55m)
Novartis exits its BioArctic BrainTransporter deal 14 months after signing
items.detail: BioArctic keeps the $30m upfront; the original deal carried up to $772m in milestones. Novartis says it dropped the program for reasons unrelated to the platform.

items.headline: Natera wins Medicare coverage for its Signatera MRD test in hepatocellular carcinoma
MediWound launches a $15m bought-deal equity offering
